exposure: Ante-partum ultrasound parameters (Head circumference (HC), Estimated Fetal Weight (EFW), Subpubic Angle (SPA))
Intra-partum ultrasound parameters (Occiput position, Head Perineum Distance (HPD), Angle of Progression (AOP))
cohort: The study participants were consecutive singleton pregnancies complicated by vacuum-assisted delivery (VD) who underwent a dedicated ultrasound assessment at 36-38 weeks of gestation.
finding: Antepartum prediction of failed vacuum-assisted delivery (VD) is feasible, with head circumference (HC) and subpubic angle (SPA) being independently associated and predictive, and a multiparametric model including maternal and intrapartum ultrasound parameters significantly improving diagnostic accuracy.
mod_finding: Antepartum ultrasound parameters, specifically head circumference (HC) and subpubic angle (SPA), along with intrapartum ultrasound and maternal characteristics, can predict the risk of failed vacuum-assisted delivery.
birth_weight: Estimated fetal weight (EFW) measured at 36-38 weeks gestation.
